items.text: Double your contributions to £600 instead of chasing a 7% return over a 5% return, because earning more and saving more is what actually moves the needle.
Until a year of market growth is bigger than a year of your contributions, you are not living off of the returns of compound interest, but just living off of your own hard work and contributions.
Do not sell at the bottom.
Stop expecting the market to make you rich.
In stage one, prioritize capital velocity by turning your time, skills, and ability to make money into money that you can invest.
Once you hit critical mass, the point where a year of market growth matches or comes close to beating a year of contribution, the game completely changes to optimization and efficiency.
Invest in an ISA or whatever tax-sheltered account exists where you live, so you can have a tax advantage where it is not going to have tax friction.
When lowering your costs, make sure it is exactly the same eggs for eggs thing that you are comparing it with.
Stop waiting for time to do the work, grow your income, push your savings rate, cut the fees, cut the tax drag, and build a critical mass, because you have to build the engine first.
